Walks a tree in pure Go and lists directory sizes up to a depth limit, sorted

largest-first. Replaces ad-hoc `du | sort | grep` for housekeeping so agents

and CI get the same behavior on macOS, Linux, and Windows.



Pair with scripts/clean-project-sprawl.sh after identifying hot spots under
.zqk/.

  Project root, depth 2, entries >= 1MiB (default)
  zqk system disk-usage
  Same shape as du -h -d 2 filtered to gigabyte-scale paths
  zqk system disk-usage --depth 2 --min 1G
  Inspect .zqk log/state sprawl
  zqk system disk-usage .zqk --depth 3 --min 10M --format json
  Top 20 hotspots anywhere under cwd
  zqk system disk-usage --top 20 --min 0

Usage:
  zqk system disk-usage [flags]

Aliases:
  disk-usage, du

Flags:
  -d, --depth int          Maximum directory depth relative to the scan root (root is 0) (default 2)
  -f, --format string      Output format (table, json, jsonl, yaml, csv, json-rpc, stream, agent-prompt, semantic-link) (default "table")
      --include-files      Also list regular files at depth <= --depth
      --min string         Only list entries at least this large (e.g. 1M, 500M, 1G, 0) (default "1M")
  -o, --output string      Write output to file
  -q, --quiet              Suppress non-essential output
      --timeout duration   Timeout for command execution (0 = auto-calculate)
      --top int            Limit to the N largest entries after filtering (0 = unlimited)
  -v, --verbose            Verbose output

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
